title: WorkflowEvent
description: Lifecycle of a multi-step workflow that spans more than one turn — a scheduled job, a long-running task, a consolidation run. A TURN IS NOT A WORKFLOW: a turn is one wake-to-speech exchange, a workflow can outlive a session and survive a restart. Conflating them is why a resumable task ends up entangled in conversation state.

compatibility.notes: PROVISIONAL. Nothing produces workflows until memory consolidation lands in Phase 2, and the shape may need to change once there is a real workload. It is defined now anyway so the Event envelope has a second specialization to prove the base is not turn-specific — a base class with one subclass is just a base class with extra steps. Promote to stable at G2.

workflow_type.description: memory_reindex is the ADR-0010 embedding-model migration — long, resumable, and the one that must never be interrupted halfway without a recovery path.

status.description: `compensating` means undoing partial work after a failure. It exists because ADR-0026 forbids abandoning a `write` mid-flight — a failed multi-step workflow must unwind, not just stop.

resumable.description: True means the workflow can survive a process restart and continue from `checkpoint`. A long workflow that is NOT resumable must be small enough to redo from scratch — otherwise a restart loses work with no way to recover.

checkpoint.description: Opaque resume state. Persisted by the owner, not by the event log.

side_effect.description: ADR-0026, applied at workflow granularity — governs whether a failure requires compensation.

error.message: Vector backend dropped mid-reindex; unwinding to the pre-migration index.
error.degraded_behavior: rolled back to the previous embedding model; recall unaffected
